witness_description: No certified counterexample: the sweep finds raw tables with f(1)=3 that violate one or more listed equalities, but the quote does not define P(n) or the admissible functions f.
refutation_explanation: A violating table can be certified only if it also satisfies whatever hypotheses P(1), P(3), P(4), and P(5) express. Since P is undefined in the supplied data, finite assignments to the displayed values of f cannot determine admissibility, so the search is inconclusive.
search_space: Exhaustively swept all 6^5 = 7776 tables assigning f(1), f(3), f(4), f(5), and f(6) values from {1,2,3,4,5,6}, in lexicographic itertools.product order; 1295 tables have f(1)=3 and violate at least one listed consequent equality. This sweep is exhaustive only for those raw tables, not for the undefined P constraints or the claim.
